title: Pestilence in the Capital
text: Sailors and carters have carried the pestilence through your gates. Black swellings appear in the poorer quarters, and the bells toll for the dead from dawn to dusk. Your physicians beg you to close the city before the sickness spreads.

choices.text: Seal the gates and quarantine the sick

title: The Pestilence Spreads
text: The sickness has escaped the capital and now runs along every road and river. Whole villages lie empty, fields go unharvested and the survivors whisper that heaven has turned its face away. Unless you act, the dying will go on all year.

choices.text: Wait for it to burn itself out

title: The Pestilence Recedes
text: No new cases have been reported for a month, and the death carts no longer rattle through the streets at night. The survivors open their shutters and count the empty houses. Your people look to you to mark the end of the dying.

choices.text: Hold a great service of thanksgiving
Offer the empty farms to settlers

title: A Wet Summer
text: It has rained since spring and the wheat is rotting in the fields. Bread prices in your towns have doubled in a month and the poor are already muttering. Your stewards ask whether you mean to feed them.

choices.text: Open your granaries to the poor
Let prices find their own level

title: Famine
text: The granaries are empty and the next harvest is months away. Families eat their seed corn, then grass and bark, and the roads fill with the hungry walking toward your towns. Every week of delay costs lives.

choices.text: Buy grain abroad at any price
Seize the stores of lords and abbeys
Let the hungry fend for themselves

title: A Golden Harvest
text: Sun and rain have come at the right times all year, and the barns cannot hold the grain. Markets overflow, bread is cheap and the villages are holding feasts. Your treasurer notes that a full harvest can bear a heavier tax.

choices.text: Let the peasants keep the surplus

title: The Villages Rise
text: Peasants armed with flails, scythes and stolen hunting spears are marching on the nearest town. They demand an end to new dues and the heads of the bailiffs who collect them. Their numbers grow at every village they pass.

choices.text: Grant them a charter of rights

title: The Towns Refuse to Pay
text: Burghers in several of your towns have shut their gates on the tax collectors and rung the alarm bells. Guild militias man the walls, and their leaders say they will pay nothing more until their old privileges are restored.

choices.text: Send soldiers to collect what is owed
Blame your treasurer and dismiss him

title: Bandits on the Roads
text: Merchants arrive at your capital stripped to their shirts, if they arrive at all. A band of former soldiers rules the forest roads, taking tolls in your name and hanging anyone who argues. Trade along the highways is drying up.

choices.text: Leave the roads to merchant guards

title: A Governor Grows Proud
text: The governor of one of your distant provinces has stopped forwarding taxes, raised his own guard and begun holding court like a prince. He still swears loyalty in every letter. Your council is divided on whether to bribe him or break him.

choices.text: Recall him and seize his estates
Let him keep his little kingdom

title: A Born Commander
text: A younger son of a minor house has won every tourney and skirmish he has entered, and the soldiers already sing about him. He asks for a real command. Your marshals grumble that he is untested and far too popular.

choices.text: Give him an army to lead
Make him master of the horse

title: A Master of Mines
text: A grizzled engineer who has dug tunnels under a dozen walls offers you his services. He brings his own miners, sappers and a chest of plans. His fee is steep, and he expects to be paid in advance.

choices.text: Give him command of an army

title: Mutiny in the Ranks
text: Your soldiers have not been paid in months, and this morning a regiment threw its officers out of camp. Other units are watching to see what you do. The mutineers say they will fight again the day their arrears are paid in full.

title: Deserters
text: Every morning the roll call comes up shorter. Homesick levies slip away at night to bring in their harvests, and some take their weapons with them. Your captains want examples made; your stewards point out that the fields need the men.

choices.text: Pay a bounty for every man returned
Let them go home to their farms

title: A Sword for Hire
text: A famous mercenary captain rides into your capital at the head of his company and offers you their services. His men are veterans, well armed and expensive. If you do not hire them, he says cheerfully, someone else surely will.

title: Weary of War
text: Widows and maimed veterans crowd your market squares, and the war taxes grow heavier every season. Preachers pray openly for peace. Your councillors warn that patience at home is running out faster than your enemies' armies.

title: Songs of Victory
text: Ballads of your victories are sung in every tavern, and foreign envoys speak of your armies with respect. Your veterans want rewarding and your people want a celebration. Neighbouring courts are watching how you carry your glory.

choices.text: Hold a triumph in the capital
Settle your veterans on public land
Boast of it at every foreign court

title: A Noble Prisoner
text: Your soldiers have captured an enemy commander of high birth, still in his gilded armour. His family will pay handsomely for his return. Some of your officers would rather see him hanged for the villages his men burned.

title: Idle Garrisons
text: With no enemy in sight, your soldiers spend their days dicing, drinking and brawling with townsfolk. Their captains want to drill them hard through the winter. Your treasurer would rather send half of them home for a season.

choices.text: Send half home on reduced pay

title: Raiders Across the Border
text: Horsemen from across the border have burned a string of your villages and driven off the cattle. Their lord claims to know nothing about it. Your frontier barons want revenge, and they would like you to lead it.

choices.text: Raid them back twice as hard

title: The Heir Falls Ill
text: Your heir has taken to bed with a burning fever, and the court physicians argue over bleeding and purges. Foreign doctors of great reputation could be summoned at great cost. Meanwhile, ambassadors are already asking pointed questions.

title: Whispers of Succession
text: Word of your heir's illness has leaked from the palace, and every tavern has its own story of poison or death. Nobles quietly weigh which cousin to back. The heir has recovered, but the damage is done.

choices.text: Show the heir at a public feast

title: Scandal at Court
text: Your favourite at court has been caught selling offices and pardons, and the whole capital knows it. The great nobles demand his head. He swears he has always been loyal to you, and he knows a great many of your secrets.

choices.text: Hand him over to his enemies
Protect him and share his takings

title: A Feud Between Great Houses
text: Two of your greatest noble families have quarrelled over a marriage contract, and now their retainers are burning each other's villages. Both houses appeal to you for justice, and both have hinted at what they will do if you rule against them.

choices.text: Judge the case yourself at court

title: A Restless Heir
text: Your heir is bored with court ceremony and has gathered a circle of young hotheads. They talk of glory, of old claims and of what they will do when their turn comes. It would be wise to give the heir something to do.

choices.text: Give the heir a frontier command
Send the heir to tour foreign courts

title: Quarrels on the Council
text: With a weak hand on the throne, your councillors no longer pretend to cooperate. The chancellor and the marshal block each other's orders, and every decision stalls. Each asks you to dismiss the other.

title: The Ruler's Health Fails
text: You now need help to climb the palace stairs and doze through council meetings. Physicians mutter about dropsy and a weak heart. Your heir waits respectfully, but the court has already begun to drift toward the rising sun.

choices.text: Carry on with the help of physicians
Abdicate in favour of your heir

title: A Marriage Proposal
text: A foreign court proposes a match between one of its princes and a daughter of your house. The alliance would bring friends abroad, but the dowry they expect is steep. Some at court think you could aim higher.

choices.text: Accept the match and pay the dowry
Hold out for a grander match

title: A Grand Tournament
text: Knights from across the land, and a few famous champions from abroad, ask you to proclaim a great tournament. There would be jousts, melees and feasting for a week, and every noble house would want a seat in the stands.

choices.text: Proclaim a tournament worthy of legend
Hold a modest contest of arms
Forbid it as a waste of good men

title: Factions in the Council
text: Your council is split between the old landed families and the newer merchant houses, and each blocks the other's bills. Votes are bought openly and armed servants follow councillors through the streets. The election is a month away.

title: An Office for Sale
text: A wealthy canon with powerful relatives offers a chest of gold for the vacant provostship of your chapter. He is ambitious, worldly and not especially devout. The older brothers are scandalised that you would even consider it.

choices.text: Give the office to a pious brother

title: The Guilds Want a Charter
text: The richest guilds of your capital offer a generous gift in return for a charter confirming their monopolies. Their goods would be shielded from foreign competition, but prices would rise and outsiders would be shut out of the trade.

choices.text: Grant the charter for their gift
Open the trades to all comers

title: A Great Fair
text: Merchants from a dozen lands ask your leave to hold a great fair outside your capital each summer. They promise cloth, spices, furs and silver, and ask only that their goods pass your tolls untaxed while the fair lasts.

choices.text: Allow it, but tax every stall

title: Silver in the Hills
text: Shepherds have found bright ore in a stream bed, and your assayers confirm a rich vein of silver. Working it will need shafts, pumps and skilled miners from abroad. Several banking houses have already offered to lease it from you.

choices.text: Work it as a state mine

title: Bankers at the Door
text: Agents of a great banking house have come to your chancery with an offer of credit, secured against your future revenues. The terms are fair for now, though interest has a way of growing. They hint that your rivals have already borrowed.

choices.text: Borrow as much as they will lend

title: Creditors at the Gates
text: Your creditors have stopped asking politely. Interest now swallows a large share of your revenues, and the bankers refuse to lend another coin until you show them you can pay. Your treasurer lays out the unpleasant options.

choices.text: Squeeze the clergy for a subsidy

title: A New Trade Route
text: One of your merchant houses has found a shorter road to a rich foreign market that avoids a rival's tolls entirely. Other merchants are clamouring to follow. The founding house asks for a monopoly on the route in return for a share of the profits.

choices.text: Open the route to every merchant

title: Smugglers' Coves
text: Your customs officers report that half the wine, salt and cloth landed on your coast never passes a toll house. Smuggling gangs run whole villages and pay the local gentry to look away. The officers want soldiers and new powers.

choices.text: Take a quiet cut of their profits

title: The Salt Trade
text: Your salt works have never produced so much, and salt is worth its weight in silver to every fisherman and butcher. Your treasurer proposes making it a state monopoly. The merchants who now handle the trade are not pleased.

choices.text: Lease the works to the merchants

title: A Splendid Yield
text: Your vineyards and orchards have given the finest yield in a generation, and foreign buyers are crowding the markets and river landings. Your stewards suggest the best of it might do more good on your own table, in front of foreign envoys.

title: Exiles Seek a Home
text: Jewish families expelled from a neighbouring kingdom ask leave to settle in your towns. They bring physicians, scholars, printers and merchants with partners in every port of the Mediterranean. Some of your preachers already rail against them.

choices.text: Admit them for a heavy fee

title: Fire in the Capital
text: A baker's oven set a thatched roof alight, and a dry wind did the rest. A third of your capital lies in ash, from the river wharves to the market square. Thousands sleep in the fields, and the guilds ask how the city will be rebuilt.

choices.text: Rebuild in stone at your expense
Rebuild on a grand new plan
Let the townsfolk rebuild as they can

title: The River Bursts Its Banks
text: After weeks of rain upstream, the river has burst its banks and drowned the low fields for miles. Mills are smashed, granaries spoiled and livestock lost. Your engineers say proper dikes would stop it happening again, if you can pay for them.

title: The Earth Shakes
text: A great earthquake has struck your lands, toppling towers and cracking town walls from end to end. Aftershocks keep the survivors sleeping in the open. Preachers proclaim it a judgement, and the homeless look to you for bread and timber.

title: The Great Bridge Falls
text: The old bridge that carried the main road over the river has collapsed under a laden wagon train, drowning carters and their teams. Trade must now wait on slow ferries. Your engineers have plans for a new bridge in stone, at a price.

choices.text: Build a grand new stone bridge

title: Wolves in Winter
text: The hardest winter in living memory has driven wolf packs down from the forests and hills. They take sheep from the folds and travellers on the roads, and villagers bar their doors at dusk. They beg you for help.

choices.text: Pay a bounty for every pelt
Lead your nobles on a great hunt
Let the villages see to it

title: Raiders on the Coast
text: Raiders from across the sea struck your coast at dawn, burning a fishing town and carrying off its people to sell in foreign markets. The survivors demand protection. Your captains say the raiders' nests could be found, if you pay for ships.

choices.text: Fit out ships to hunt them
Let the coast fend for itself

title: Storm at Sea
text: A sudden gale has scattered your fleet along a hostile coast. Several ships ran aground and others limped home with shattered masts and drowned crews. Your admiral blames the pilots; the pilots blame the admiral.

choices.text: Pay for the repairs at once

title: Refugees at the Border
text: Thousands of families fleeing a war in a neighbouring land have crossed into your territory with their carts and cattle. They ask for land to farm and protection from the soldiers who burned their homes. Your own peasants eye them warily.

choices.text: Turn them back at the border

title: A Comet in the Sky
text: A star with a burning tail hangs over your lands each night, brighter than the moon. Preachers call it a warning of plague and war; your astrologers insist it heralds a triumph. The common people wait to hear what you say it means.

choices.text: Proclaim it a sign of your coming glory
Have your scholars chart its path

title: The Astrologer's Prophecy
text: Your court astrologer has cast your horoscope and announces that the stars favour a great victory before the year is out. He has told half the court already. The soldiers are delighted; your more sober advisers are not.

choices.text: Reward him and spread the news

title: The Alchemist
text: A learned stranger with stained fingers swears he is one step from turning lead into gold. He asks only for a laboratory, a furnace and a modest stipend. Your treasurer rolls his eyes, but your curiosity is harder to dismiss.

title: Gold, of a Sort
text: Your alchemist has not made gold, but his furnaces have produced something almost as useful: a finer gunpowder and a hard white glaze that potters would kill for. He begs for more funding to finish the great work.

title: A University for Your Realm
text: Scholars and doctors of law petition you to found a university in your capital. They promise lawyers for your courts, physicians for your household and learned clerks for your chancery. They need buildings, salaries and a charter under your seal.

choices.text: Let the religious houses fund it

title: A Painter Seeks Patronage
text: A painter praised in every court has arrived with letters of introduction and a folio of sketches. He asks for a salary, a workshop and a great commission worthy of his talent. Rival courts are bidding for him too.

choices.text: Commission a great work for the capital
Have him paint portraits for envoys
Let a rival court have him

title: An Envoy from Afar
text: An envoy from a realm few of your courtiers could find on a map has arrived with gifts of strange beasts, silks and spices. He has travelled for two years and wishes to learn about your country. The whole capital turns out to watch his procession.

choices.text: Ask him about the roads he travelled

title: A Spy Unmasked
text: Your guards have caught a foreign agent copying letters in your chancery. Under questioning he names his employers and offers to tell much more in exchange for his life. His masters will certainly deny knowing him.

choices.text: Execute him in the public square

title: Your Envoys Grow Nervous
text: Your ambassadors report that foreign courts speak of you with alarm. Old enemies are exchanging envoys, and treaties are being drafted that do not mention your name. Your chancellor urges you to calm the waters before a coalition forms.

choices.text: Send lavish gifts to wary courts

title: A New Cathedral
text: Your bishops present plans for a great cathedral whose spire would be seen for a day's ride. It will take generations to finish, and the masons want paying from the first stone. The clergy say a realm without such a church shames itself before God.

choices.text: Pay for it from the treasury

title: A Great Mosque
text: Your architects present plans for a congregational mosque with a dome to rival any in the world and minarets seen from the hills. Its endowments would also fund a school, a hospital and a kitchen for the poor. The cost would be enormous.

choices.text: Build it in the grandest style

title: Zealous Preachers
text: A band of fiery preachers is touring your towns, calling on the faithful to purge sin at home and take up arms against unbelievers abroad. Crowds follow them from market to market. Foreign merchants have begun closing their shops early.

choices.text: Channel their zeal into the army
Let them preach as they please

title: Monks Against the Town
text: The abbot of a rich monastery and the burghers of the neighbouring town are at each other's throats over mill rights and market tolls. Brawls break out every market day. Both sides have sent delegations to your court with gifts and petitions.

title: A Witch Accused
text: Villagers have dragged a midwife before the local court, accusing her of souring milk and causing a neighbour's death. Half the village swears to her guilt and the other half keeps silent. The judge writes to ask what you wish done.

choices.text: Let the trial run its course

title: A Preacher Against the Clergy
text: A wandering preacher draws crowds of thousands by denouncing fat abbots, sold pardons and priests with mistresses. He reads scripture aloud in the common tongue in open fields. Your bishops demand that you arrest him.

choices.text: Hand him over to the bishops
Use his sermons to tax the abbeys

title: The Papal Legate
text: A papal legate has arrived in your capital with a train of clerks, asking for a tithe on your clergy to fund the defence of Christendom. He hints that the Holy Father remembers generous sons. He also hints at what happens to the other kind.

title: A Holy Fool
text: A barefoot holy fool in iron chains has taken up his post in your capital's market and rails against your officials by name. The crowds revere him as a man of God who cannot be silenced. Several of the officials he names are indeed corrupt.

choices.text: Have him carried out of the city

title: A Pious Endowment
text: A wealthy widow has endowed a madrasa, a hospital and a public fountain in your capital, and the people bless her name in the mosques. Your religious scholars suggest you match her generosity. Your treasurer suggests otherwise.

choices.text: Match her gift with your own
Place her endowment under state control

title: Pastors at Odds
text: Your pastors have met in synod and spent a month quarrelling over the Lord's Supper, predestination and the cut of vestments. Pamphlets fly between the factions and congregations split. Both sides demand that you settle the matter.

choices.text: Impose a single confession by law
Let each parish follow its conscience

title: An Estate Without an Heir
text: One of your wealthiest lords has died without children, and three cousins are suing for his lands in your courts. By old law the estate could revert to you. The other nobles are watching closely to see whether their own lands are safe.

choices.text: Sell it to the highest bidder
Award it to the eldest cousin

title: The Printing Press
text: A printer from the Rhineland has set up a press with movable metal type in your capital. In a week he turns out more books than a monastery of scribes copies in a year. Your clergy fear what cheap books will do to common minds.

title: The Gunfounders
text: Gunfounders who learned their trade casting church bells offer to make you great bombards of bronze and iron. They promise that walls which once held out for a year will fall in weeks. Your knights call the guns a coward's weapon.

choices.text: Cast a train of siege bombards

title: Harness of Steel
text: Armourers in Milan and Augsburg now forge full harness of tempered steel, so well fitted that a knight can mount without help. Your nobles want it, but the best suits cost as much as a farm. They ask whether you will help them pay.

choices.text: Let the nobles pay their own way

title: An Order of Chivalry
text: Your heralds propose founding an order of knighthood under your patronage, with a collar, a chapel and a feast day of its own. Membership would bind your greatest nobles to you with honour rather than gold. Every lord left out will feel the slight.

choices.text: Found an order of royal knights
Dedicate the order to holy war
Leave knighthood to the old ways

title: The New Learning
text: Scholars trained in Italy arrive with Greek manuscripts and a passion for Cicero's Latin. They write elegant letters, edit ancient texts and argue that a prince should be educated like a philosopher. They are also looking for employment.

title: Painters of a New Style
text: A new school of painters has learned to show depth, light and living faces as if seen through a window. Princes and bankers compete for their brushes. Your court could have its own masterpieces, if you are willing to pay for genius.

choices.text: Keep to the old devotional masters

title: Walls Against Cannon
text: Your engineers warn that tall medieval walls shatter like pottery under modern guns. They propose low, thick ramparts with angled bastions so that every face is covered by fire. It is an untried idea, and your old castellans scoff at it.

choices.text: Trust the walls of your fathers

title: Companies Without a War
text: A truce elsewhere has left whole mercenary companies without employers, and one of them has camped on your border. Their captain offers a long contract at a fair price. If no one hires them, they will feed themselves from your villages.

title: The Caravel
text: Your shipwrights have built a small, nimble ship with lateen sails that can beat into the wind and ride out ocean swells. Pilots say it could reach coasts no one in your land has seen. Merchants and admirals both want the first of them.

title: A Call for Crusade
text: The Pope has proclaimed a crusade against the Turks, and preachers in every parish urge the faithful to take the cross. Pardons are promised to all who fight or pay. Your own nobles are torn between piety and prudence.

title: The First Pike Squares
text: Your new companies of pikemen and gunners are the talk of every court in Europe. Foreign officers come to watch them drill, and your recruiting sergeants are turning men away. For a time, at least, no army is more modern than yours.
news: Word spreads of a realm whose pike squares are the most modern army in Europe.

choices.text: Show them off in a grand review

title: Prices Keep Rising
text: Silver pours into Europe from mines old and new, and every year bread, wool and iron cost more. Your fixed rents and old tolls buy less each season while merchants grow rich. Your treasurer says the old revenues cannot keep up.

choices.text: Debase the coin to keep pace

title: Fortresses of the New Style
text: Italian engineers now build star-shaped fortresses whose low bastions shrug off cannon fire and sweep every ditch with crossfire. A single such fortress can hold an army at bay for a season. They cost a fortune and take years to finish.

choices.text: Ring your frontier with star forts

title: Soldiers Who Stay
text: Your captains argue that levies called up for each campaign are no match for professionals who drill all year. They want permanent companies, paid even in peacetime. The cost would be ruinous, but so is losing battles.

title: Instruments of Navigation
text: Pilots now cross open ocean using the astrolabe, the cross-staff and charts drawn from careful observation. Foreign captains guard their secrets jealously. A school for pilots would give your sailors the same skills, at a price.

title: Reformers in Your Pulpits
text: Preachers inspired by the reformers in the Empire now fill your churches, denouncing the Pope, the sale of pardons and the wealth of the monasteries. Townsmen sing hymns in their own tongue. Your bishops demand action; your treasurer eyes the abbey lands.

choices.text: Burn their books and silence them

title: The Society of Jesus
text: Disciplined priests of a new order offer to open colleges in your towns, teaching Latin, mathematics and rhetoric free of charge. They are superb teachers and fierce defenders of Rome. Some at court whisper that they answer to no prince.

choices.text: Keep them out of your schools

title: Decrees of the Council
text: The great council of the Church has finished its work, ordering bishops to live in their dioceses, a seminary in every see and an end to the worst abuses. Rome asks every Catholic prince to publish the decrees. Your own clergy are not eager to reform.

choices.text: Publish them but reserve your rights

title: Armies Grow Larger
text: Across Europe, armies have doubled in size within living memory, and gunpowder decides more battles than lances. Princes who cannot field tens of thousands of men are swept aside. Your marshals ask whether you will keep pace.

title: Architects from Italy
text: Architects trained in Rome and Florence offer to rebuild your residence with columns, loggias and gardens in the antique style. Ambassadors judge a ruler by their house, they remind you. The work would take a decade and empty a treasury.

choices.text: Build a palace in the new style
Add a new wing and gardens

title: A Postal Service
text: A family of couriers offers to run relays of riders along your main roads, carrying letters from frontier to capital in days rather than weeks. They want a monopoly on the service. Your governors would at last hear your orders before events overtake them.

choices.text: Run the post as a state service
Let letters travel as they always have

title: The First Pike and Shot Army
text: Your musketeers, pikemen and light field guns now fight as a single machine, and foreign generals ride a hundred miles to watch your manoeuvres. Rival courts are hurrying to copy you. The advantage will not last, but it is yours today.
news: Word spreads of a realm whose musketeers and field guns have rewritten the art of war.

choices.text: Hold a great review for the envoys

title: Drill and Volley
text: Officers schooled in the ancient manuals have devised a drill in which ranks of musketeers fire, step back and reload in turn, keeping up an unbroken rain of shot. It demands endless practice and veteran sergeants. Armies that master it win battles.

choices.text: Drill the whole army the new way
Keep faith in the cavalry charge

title: The Witch Craze
text: A panic over witchcraft has spread from village to village. Every failed harvest or stillborn calf brings a new accusation, and confessions extracted by torture name ever more neighbours. Your judges ask whether the trials should continue.

choices.text: Let the courts root out the witches

title: The Cold Years
text: Winters have grown longer and harsher for a generation. Frost comes in May, rivers freeze hard enough to hold fairs on the ice, and harvests fail one year in three. Your stewards say the old farming calendar no longer serves.

title: A Bank of Exchange
text: Merchants propose a public bank that would hold deposits, settle bills and lend to the state at low interest, all guaranteed by your treasury. Such banks have made other cities rich. If it fails, your credit fails with it.

choices.text: Keep the bankers at arm's length

title: Lands Stripped Bare
text: Years of marching armies, friend and foe alike, have stripped your countryside bare. Villages stand empty, fields go back to forest and wolves roam where farms once stood. Your soldiers now forage in lands that have nothing left to give.

choices.text: Let the armies take what they need

title: Secretaries of State
text: Your government has outgrown a council of nobles and a handful of clerks. Your chancellor proposes permanent ministries with salaried secretaries, registries and written procedures. The great nobles who ran things by favour will lose influence.

choices.text: Sell offices to fund the state

title: Music Drama
text: Composers have invented a new art in which whole dramas are sung, with stage machines that lower gods from painted clouds. Every great court now wants its own theatre. Your nobles would sit through anything to be seen there with you.

title: The War Contractor
text: A ruthless nobleman offers to raise and equip an entire army at his own expense. In return he wants the right to levy contributions from every district his troops pass through, yours included. His armies are formidable; his methods are brutal.

choices.text: Hire a smaller force on your terms

title: Neighbours Divided by Faith
text: Catholics and Protestants now live street by street in your towns, and every feast day risks a riot. Preachers on both sides call the others servants of the devil. Moderates beg you to proclaim a peace of religion before blood is spilled.

title: A Congress of Peace
text: Diplomats from across Europe are gathering in a neutral city to end a generation of war. They speak of a balance of power and of princes who answer to no one within their own lands. Every realm that sends envoys will have a voice.

title: Through the Glass
text: A lens-grinder's tube reveals mountains on the moon, spots on the sun and new stars beyond counting. Your scholars clamour for an observatory, while some churchmen warn that the new astronomy contradicts scripture.

title: The First Modern Army
text: Your battalions in uniform coats march in step, fire by platoon and manoeuvre as one body under officers who have studied their trade. Military observers from every court take notes. Your army is, for now, the model for all of Europe.
news: One European realm has fielded the first army of line infantry, and the rest of the continent hurries to follow.

title: A Palace to Dazzle Europe
text: Your architects present plans for a vast palace outside the capital, with a mile of gardens, galleries of mirrors and apartments for a thousand courtiers. Nobles who live under your eye cannot plot in their provinces. The price is staggering.

choices.text: Build it and summon the nobles to court

title: The Coffee Houses
text: Coffee houses have opened in your capital, where merchants strike deals, scholars argue and gossip travels faster than any courier. For a penny anyone can read the newsletters and talk politics. Your ministers suspect the talk is not always loyal.

choices.text: Close them as dens of sedition

title: Salons and Philosophers
text: In the salons of your capital, hostesses gather writers who question every tradition, from the rights of rulers to the miracles of saints. Their books are read across Europe. Some would gladly praise an enlightened patron; others write as if no ruler deserved one.

title: An Academy of Sciences
text: Natural philosophers propose an academy under your patronage where they could test ideas by experiment, publish their findings and advise your ministers on mines, canals and gunnery. Rival courts have founded such bodies already. Its members expect salaries and a fine building.

choices.text: Grant a charter but no funds

title: A Great Canal
text: Your engineers propose a canal with locks and aqueducts to join two rivers, so that barges could carry grain and timber across your lands at a fraction of the cost by road. It would take ten thousand labourers and a decade of work.

title: A Chartered Company
text: Merchants propose a joint-stock company with a charter to trade in distant seas, armed ships of its own and shares sold to anyone with savings. They ask you for the charter and invite you to buy shares. Such companies have made fortunes, and lost them.

choices.text: Grant it and buy a large stake
Keep the seas open to all

title: The Company Pays Out
text: Your company's ships have returned laden with spices, silks and porcelain, and the directors declare a dividend that makes your stake worth several times its price. The court talks of nothing else. Shareholders are already pressing for a second voyage.

title: A School for Officers
text: Your generals complain that officers who bought their commissions cannot read a map or site a battery. They propose an academy where young nobles would learn mathematics, fortification and drill before they lead a single company.

title: Counting the People
text: Your ministers want to know exactly how many subjects you have, what they own and what they could pay. A census would send clerks into every parish to count hearths, cattle and men of fighting age. Your people fear new taxes will follow the counting.

title: State Manufactories
text: Your ministers propose state workshops for glass, tapestry, silk and porcelain, staffed by craftsmen lured from abroad. Every luxury made at home is gold that stays in the realm. Private merchants protest that the state should not compete with them.

title: The Socket Bayonet
text: A simple ring that fixes a blade beside the muzzle lets every musketeer be his own pikeman and still fire. Your generals predict the end of the pike. Re-arming a whole army, however, means new muskets, new drill and a great deal of money.

choices.text: Re-arm the entire army at once
